faq.q: Is October a good time for a boat rental in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, October is one of the best shoulder-season months. Air temperatures average 22–28°C, sea water is still around 20°C, and the summer crowds have gone. You'll find more space at anchorages like Cala del Faro and easier berthing at Puerto Banús. Just bring a light jacket for the breeze.

faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella in October 2044?
faq.a: Expect mostly sunny days with occasional short showers (average rainfall ~40mm). Sea breezes pick up in the afternoon, so plan morning departures for calmest conditions. Water temperature hovers around 20°C, so you can still swim if you're brave — a wetsuit helps.

faq.q: Which boats are available for charter in October?
faq.a: Our entire fleet operates year-round from Puerto Banús. For small groups, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are ideal. For larger parties, the Astondoa 40 (9 pax) or Azimut 39 (11 pax) offer great value. Luxury options like the Mangusta 80 or Ferretti 94 are also available.

faq.q: How much does a boat rental cost in October?
faq.a: Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, with skipper, drinks, and VAT included. The Mangusta 80 (including the grey variant) starts at €4,719 for a 4-hour charter, which includes a jet ski. Other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance for October?
faq.a: While October is quieter, weekends and sunny days can still fill up. We recommend booking 1–2 weeks ahead to secure your preferred boat and time slot. Last-minute bookings are often possible, especially mid-week, but check availability via WhatsApp.

faq.q: What should I wear on a boat in October?
faq.a: Layers are key: a light jumper or windbreaker for the sea breeze, plus sunglasses and sunscreen (UV is still strong). If you plan to swim, bring a towel and maybe a thin wetsuit — sea temp is around 20°C. Non-slip shoes are a good idea on deck.

faq.q: Can we still swim and do water sports in October?
faq.a: Yes, but the water is cooler (20°C) than in summer. Many guests swim briefly or use the included jet ski (on Mangusta charters). For longer swims, a wetsuit is recommended. Anchorages like Cala Cortés are sheltered and often calmer in autumn.

data.body_html:
October in Marbella is the sweet spot of the shoulder season — the summer heat has softened, the crowds have thinned, and the Mediterranean still holds a pleasant 20°C. If you’re considering a Marbella boat rental in October 2044, you’re in for a more relaxed, authentic experience than any July day. Here’s everything you need to know to plan your charter.

Why October is a Smart Choice for a Boat Charter

October offers the best of both worlds: warm enough for sunbathing on deck, but without the intense 35°C heat of August. Average air temperatures range from 22°C to 28°C, and the sea is still swimmable, especially with a light wetsuit. The shoulder season means fewer boats at anchor, easier booking, and more attentive service. You’ll find Puerto Banús less frantic, yet all restaurants and beach clubs remain open.

October Weather and Sea Conditions in Marbella

Expect mostly sunny days with a 20% chance of a brief shower — annual October rainfall is around 40mm, so it’s not a washout. Winds are typically light to moderate (10–15 knots), with mornings calmer than afternoons. Sea temperature hovers near 20°C, perfect for a quick dip or paddleboarding. Always check the marine forecast before departure; our skippers know the local microclimates well.

Which Boat to Choose for Your October Charter

Our fleet covers every group size and budget. For an intimate outing, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) are nimble and affordable. For families or friends, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are the most popular — both start at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for a full day. If you want luxury, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) or its grey variant start at €4,719 for 4 hours, with a jet ski thrown in.

Pricing and What’s Included on Every Charter

Transparent pricing is our policy. Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are €749/2h or €2,299/8h. The Mangusta 80 (white or grey) is €4,719 for a minimum 4h, including a jet ski. All other boats are priced on request via WhatsApp — no hidden fees. Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). That means you pay one price and nothing extra.

Best Routes and Destinations for October Cruising

With calmer seas, October is ideal for exploring the coastline. Head east to Cala del Faro for a sheltered swim stop, or west to Cala Cortés — a favourite for its crystal-clear water. If you have time, cruise to Estepona or even Sotogrande for lunch. For a shorter trip, stay close to Puerto Banús and anchor off the Golden Mile for a sunset view of La Concha mountain. Our skippers know the best spots for the season.

Tips for a Perfect October Charter

  • Book morning departures (9–11am) for the calmest sea and best light.
  • Bring layers — a light jacket is essential for the ride back.
  • Apply reef-safe sunscreen; UV is still strong in October.
  • Ask about the jet ski on Mangusta charters — it’s included free.
  • Reserve a table at a beach club like Ocean Club or Nikki Beach for a post-cruise lunch.

How to Book Your October Charter

Booking is simple: visit our main page to browse the fleet, then contact us via WhatsApp for availability and pricing on non-tier boats. For Tier A and Mangusta, you can book directly online. October is shoulder season, so you’ll find flexibility — but popular weekends still fill fast. Secure your spot 1–2 weeks in advance for the best choice.
